item.title: Nuclei on the Light Front and Electron Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.37811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops relativistic nuclear structure, motivated by past, current and future experi- ments at Jefferson Lab and the Electron-Ion Collider. Building on existing tools from conventional nuclear physics, we reformulate them in a relativistic, light-front-quantized framework. Our light- front nuclear structure calculations reproduce nuclear binding energies and shell structure well, and incorporate the physics of nucleon-nucleon short-ranged-correlations (SRCs) through similarity renormalization group techniques. Our results are that a purely nucleonic description is insufficient to capture inclusive electron-nucleus scattering data. It does not fully reproduce the plateaus seen at high Bjorken-xB, pointing to the importance of non-nucleonic dynamics responsible for the EMC effect
item.dc:creator: Dmitriy N. Kim, Gerald A. Miller

item.title: Orientation effects of deformed nuclei in intermediate-energy nuclear scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.38132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effects of nuclear deformation on intermediate-energy nuclear scattering within the Glauber theory. A formalism that explicitly incorporates the orientation dependence of deformed intrinsic states is derived, in which reaction observables are first computed with a fixed orientation and then the angle average of the reaction observables is taken afterwards. This formalism is applied to elastic scattering and total reaction cross sections. In addition, a new expansion scheme of the optical-limit approximation is proposed and shown to include contributions from a class of nuclear excitations, allowing a simple estimate of part of the total inelastic scattering cross section. The orientation dependence is generally weak for both proton- and carbon-target scattering and supports the validity of conventional treatments with an angle averaged density for light and medium-heavy nuclei. However, noticeable deviations emerge for strongly deformed heavy nuclei. The present analysis further demonstrates that the summed inelastic scattering cross section to rotationally excited states can be interpreted as a manifestation of fluctuations of the nuclear surface density associated with deformation. The present study provides a quantum-mechanical interpretation of deformation effects in intermediate-energy nuclear reactions and suggests a pathway toward a more reliable theoretical description of interaction cross section measurements. Brief comments on the role of nuclear deformation in low-energy heavy-ion reactions and ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions are also made.
item.dc:creator: W. Horiuchi, K. Hagino

item.title: Quantum Correlations Between Two Giant Dipole Resonances in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mutual Coulomb dissociation in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions is dominated by Giant Dipole Resonance (GDR) excitation, whose subsequent decays produce forward neutrons. Standard descriptions treat the two GDRs excited in opposite nuclei as statistically independent, leading primarily to a quadrupolar azimuthal correlation determined by the common photon-polarization axis. In this work, we investigate the possibility that the two GDRs are instead prepared with a correlated quantum phase during the overlap of the electromagnetic pulses. We develop a phase-sensitive GDR decay model and implement it in a modified version of the \texttt{$n_{0}^{0}n$} Monte Carlo generator, allowing a quantitative comparison among three competing mechanisms: the weak dipolar modulation from electromagnetic recoil, the quadrupolar correlation from independent polarized GDR decays, and the phase-sensitive dipolar modulation associated with the proposed phase-lock scenario. For neutron pairs with small relative emission-time differences, the correlated-phase scenario produces a pronounced first-harmonic modulation in the two-neutron relative-azimuth distribution. Averaging over all relative emission times substantially reduces this modulation. Within the adopted energy-dependent angular model, the time-selected dipolar coefficient increases in magnitude with pair-mean neutron kinetic energy. These results identify neutron relative-azimuth correlations and their energy dependence as experimentally accessible observables for probing quantum phase correlations between the two GDR excitations. Such phase-sensitive correlations could also provide a basis for future tests of quantum entanglement between spatially separated GDR excitations at RHIC and the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Albandry Alshammri, Ashik Ikbal Sheikh, Declan Keane, Prithwish Tribedy, Gang Wang, Zhangbu Xu, Jie Zhao

item.title: Glauber Description of Reaction Cross Sections with Bogoliubov Many-Body Wave Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I developed a microscopic framework that connects relativistic nuclear density functional theory to high-energy reaction observables by incorporating many-body Bogoliubov wavefunctions, represented in Pfaffian form, into the Monte Carlo integration of the Glauber model. This approach enables a simultaneous treatment of nuclear pairing correlations and multiple-scattering effects beyond the optical limit approximation (OLA). The method is applied to reaction cross sections of even-even O, Ne, and Mg isotopes on a $^{12}$C target. Complete multiple-scattering calculations systematically reduce the cross sections relative to the OLA and improves the agreement with measured interaction cross sections. Applications to the deformed Ne and Mg isotopes show that calculations based on a single intrinsic orientation depend strongly on the angle between the nuclear symmetry axis and the beam direction. Angular-momentum projection removes the spurious dependence on the arbitrarily selected intrinsic orientation and produces smooth isotopic systematics for the laboratory-frame cross sections. This work establishes a microscopic bridge between relativistic nuclear structure theory and reaction dynamics, providing a general framework for exploring exotic phenomena such as halos and clustering.
item.dc:creator: Jie Zhao

item.title: Disentangling the neutron skin of $^{48}$Ca from nuclear radius effects through $^{48}$Ca+$^{48}$Ca and $^{48}$Ti+$^{48}$Ti flow observables
item.description: arXiv:2610.38424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thickness of the neutron skin ($\Delta r_{np}$) in $^{48}$Ca remains uncertain. CREX and ab initio calculations point to a thin skin, while many energy density functionals prefer larger values. Relativistic heavy-ion collisions can probe the skin through its geometric imprint on the quark-gluon plasma, but a thicker skin also changes the overall nuclear size, so the two effects are hard to separate. We resolve this by systematically comparing $^{48}$Ca+$^{48}$Ca and $^{48}$Ti+$^{48}$Ti collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV using the AMPT model with string melting. For $^{48}$Ca, we take a zero-skin baseline and skins at the CREX lower and upper bounds. As size references, we add $^{48}$Ti and a skin-free $^{48}$Ca with the same density parameters as $^{48}$Ti, which separates size from skin effects. The sensitivity to the $^{48}$Ti radius is tested using two choices for its Woods-Saxon radius, one of which reproduces the experimental rms radius. We find that the neutron skin is a purely geometric perturbation; the medium's transport response coefficients are unchanged, first-moment observables exhibit only modest sensitivity to $\Delta r_{np}$, while second-moment observables respond much more strongly. The final-state covariance between flow and mean transverse momentum fluctuations, with its normalized correlation, is the most promising measurable probe. The radius-matched $^{48}$Ca follows $^{48}$Ti closely, and the position of $^{48}$Ti relative to the skin configurations depends on its radius. These collisions, analyzed with second-moment and shape-size correlators, offer a promising independent constraint on the $^{48}$Ca neutron skin at the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Abhisek Saha

item.title: An Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.38780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emulating the Green's function using reduced-order equations is challenging because of the amount of information it contains. This information includes the one-particle spectroscopy over the entire energy spectrum, the one-body density matrix, and the ground-state energy. Nevertheless, the computational speedup offered by emulators is essential for applications requiring repeated model evaluations, which are ubiquitous in many-body physics. These include parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, phase-diagram mapping, and geometry optimization. In this Letter, we introduce a systematically improvable emulator based on eigenvector continuation and moment-matching. The resulting approximation, which we refer to as an ``eigenvector-continued Green's function,'' can be obtained by solving linear equations, enabling an efficient separation of the computational workload into offline and online stages.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Brolli, Carlo Barbieri

item.title: Ab Initio Calculations of $^6$He + $p$ Reactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The no-core shell model with continuum (NCSMC) is an ab initio framework for description of nuclear structure and reactions. Recent developments of the NCSMC allow for calculations of charge-exchange and nucleon-transfer reactions. We have applied the NCSMC to calculate cross sections of the ($p,p$), ($p,n$), and ($p,t$) reactions on radioactive $^6$He, using chiral nuclear forces as input.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Herko, Petr Navr\'atil, Konstantinos Kravvaris, Sofia Quaglioni, Guillaume Hupin

item.title: Configuration-Interaction Studies of Alpha Clustering in Atomic Nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.39036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clustering in atomic nuclei, and $\alpha$ clustering in particular, is a striking form of self-organization in quantum many-body systems, emerging from nucleon--nucleon interactions through the interplay of correlations, symmetry constraints, and continuum coupling. We summarize a configuration-interaction approach in which cluster degrees of freedom are built from center-of-mass boosted fragment wave functions and treated with resonating-group techniques. The norm kernel plays an important role: Pauli blocking suppresses cluster channels at small separations, restructures the relative-motion wave functions, and governs the normalization of clustering strength. As the central development we present a Green's function (GF) method that aids in resolving a long-standing difficulty of harmonic-oscillator based configuration interaction calculations that stems from wave functions with Gaussian asymptotics. The method restores the correct asymptotic behavior and extracts the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) with high accuracy even in very modest harmonic-oscillator spaces. The value of the ANC is very sensitive to the exact position of the state relative to threshold, and yet the GF method establishes the ANC as a structural observable that can be determined precisely from the interior wave function using the experimentally or otherwise known exact energy. A self-consistent iteration, formulated as an integral-operator eigenvalue problem, is also shown to recover both the energy and the ANC in cases when the energy of the state is to be determined. The method is illustrated for near-threshold states, such as the weakly bound $1^-$ state of $^{16}$O, as well as for the ground states of $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne.
item.dc:creator: Brandon Roldan Tomei, Alexander Volya

item.title: Enhanced structure-dependent alpha decay tunneling in deformed odd-odd nuclei via intense two-color laser pulses
item.description: arXiv:2610.39203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present work, we investigate the effect of ultra-intense laser fields on the $\alpha$ decay tunneling of deformed odd-odd nuclei. Calculations performed within the deformed density-dependent cluster model show that, for deformed odd-odd $\alpha$ emitters, the laser-induced variation in the penetration probability separates into distinct branches associated with different valence particle-hole configurations relative to the $Z=82$ and $N=126$ shell closures. In contrast to the even-even and odd-$A$ cases, the odd-odd parent nucleus most sensitive to the laser field is not the one with the lowest $\alpha$ decay energy. This indicates that the laser response is governed not only by $Q_{\alpha}$ but also by structural correlations associated with the simultaneously unpaired proton and neutron. We further examine the pulse-averaged response under a two-color laser field. The results show that an optimized two-color field enhances the pulse-averaged laser response for most of the studied nuclei, while highly sensitive nuclei exhibit an effective gain equivalent to increasing the laser intensity by more than one order of magnitude. These findings identify structural determinants of laser-assisted $\alpha$ decay in odd-odd nuclei and provide guidance for selecting candidate nuclei and optimizing laser parameters in future experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jun-Hao Cheng, Qiong Xiao, Liang Gao, Tong-Pu Yu

item.title: Effects of the $a_0(980)$ Meson on Finite Nuclei in a Parity Doublet Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.39245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate nuclear structure within the parity doublet model (PDM), with particular emphasis on the role of the isovector-scalar $a_0(980)$ meson. We adopt the models with and without the $a_0$ meson and fit their parameters to nuclear matter saturation and ground state properties of selected nuclei, subject to constraints from the vacuum. The resulting parameter sets reproduce the nuclear matter saturation properties and provide a good description of binding energies and charge radii of selected nuclei. Our fits show that a large value of the chiral invariant mass of nucleon is preferred by the fitting: the best fitted value is $m_0 = 689 \pm 71 $ MeV with $a_0$ and $m_0 = 689 \pm 69 $ MeV without $a_0$. We find that the effects of the $a_0$ meson on the binding energies and charge radii are negligibly small. It is difficult to clarify the effect of $a_0$ meson to neutron skin thickness of Sn, Pb, and Ca isotopes, due to the large uncertainty of the predictions. We note that our prediction of $^{208} \text{Pb}$ is consistent with the measurement by PREX-II collaboration, while that of $^{48} \text{Ca}$ cannot explain the CREX result.
item.dc:creator: Yuk Kei Kong, Youngman Kim, Masayasu Harada

item.title: Irreducible representations of $SU(3)$ for nucleons in a oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$: Application to nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.39357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying some simple rules, established in group theory literature, generated are codes (easy to modify as required) for obtaining $SU(3)$ irreducible representations (irreps) for a given number of nucleons in a given oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$. In this approach, first the $SU(3)$ irreps are obtained for spinless fermions in a given $\eta$ shell. Using the codes developed, tables of $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for identical nucleons (protons or neutrons) with a given total spin $S$. Similarly, the $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for nucleons with a given spin-isospin $SU(4)$ irrep. Some applications of these tables for $\eta=4$ shell for $52 \le \mbox{Z,N} \le 78$ nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry are presented. Also, the procedure used for the shell model $SU(3)$ limits is easy to be extended for the $SU(3)$ limit of various interacting boson models and some examples for these are also presented.
item.dc:creator: V. K. B. Kota

item.title: Glashow-Weinberg relation in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.39588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The conservation of the axial-vector currents in nuclear matter with finite isospin asymmetry $\rho_n/\rho_p$ is explored in this paper. In explicit calculations in the in-medium chiral perturbation theory, a charged pion becomes massive in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter. In the presence of the massive charged pion, two components of the axial-vector current are not conserved from the two-loop order when applying the massive in-medium pion state. As a result, the in-medium Glashow-Weinberg relation for the charged pions cannot be derived in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter from operator relations in quantum chromodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Kihong Kwon, Daisuke Jido, Yamato Suda

item.title: Deposition of $\alpha$ clusters on the surface of $^{28}$Si
item.description: arXiv:2610.39878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The possibility of the appearance of the clustering structure in the surface is one of the key features determining the nuclear structural properties. In this work, we study the ground-state structure of $^{28}\text{Si}$ using the antisymmetrized quasicluster model (AQCM), focusing on the deposition of the $\alpha$ cluster structure on the surface. Three candidate structural configurations constrained to reproduce the experimental charge radius are investigated based on the $\text{SU}(3)$ shell model, the $j$-$j$ coupling shell model, and a localized $7\alpha$ cluster model. Using Glauber-model calculations for intermediate-energy proton elastic scattering, we demonstrate that the angular distribution at and beyond the first diffraction peak is highly sensitive to surface diffuseness, and that the $7\alpha$ cluster model configuration best reproduces the experimental data due to its sharper surface profile. Also, the elastic charge form factors from electron scattering support the existence of the cluster-induced oblately deformed structure.
item.dc:creator: W. Horiuchi, N. Itagaki, Y. Yamaguchi

item.title: Learning nuclear mass systematics with hybrid quantum-classical mixtures of experts
item.description: arXiv:2610.40022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a mixture-of-experts framework combining sixteen hybrid quantum-classical neural networks with nucleus-dependent classical gating to learn residual corrections to the WS4 nuclear mass model. On a fixed AME2020 test set, the framework reduces the root-mean-square error from 456.22 to 179.83 keV and outperforms a parameter-matched classical counterpart. The learned corrections improve shell-gap systematics near the Sn and Pb shell closures, while analysis of the gating networks identifies shell-related descriptors as the leading inputs. For 66Ca, the model predicts Sn = 0.577 MeV and S2n = -0.252 MeV, allowing two-neutron emission while the one-neutron channel remains closed.
item.dc:creator: Shijiang Ji, Heyi Yang, Zu-Xing Yang, Xiao-Hua Fan, Zhi-Pan Li, Haozhao Liang

item.title: Comments on $\bf{\eta'}$ nuclei and on the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton
item.description: arXiv:2610.40173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $\eta'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $\eta'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_\Lambda}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_\Lambda}^7}$He, not from ${{_\Lambda}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.
item.dc:creator: Avraham Gal

item.title: Testing thermal equilibrium in heavy-ion collisions with electric-charge fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37829v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions exhibit several phenomena commonly associated with the formation of a thermalized quark--gluon plasma. However, the observation of similar phenomena in small systems, and their non-thermal microscopic descriptions there, raises questions about this assumption. Recent continuum-extrapolated lattice-QCD calculations of the second- and fourth-order electric-charge susceptibilities, $\chi_{2}^{\Delta Q}$ and $\chi_{4}^{\Delta Q}$, reveal a striking tension with hadron-resonance-gas expectations, particularly for $\chi_{4}^{\Delta Q}$. As the ratio $\chi_{4}^{\Delta Q}/\chi_{2}^{\Delta Q}$ is experimentally measurable with net-charge cumulants, this opens up completely new ways to test whether thermal QCD applies in central heavy-ion collisions. However, achieving a measurement that can be interpreted with high precision requires further work on both the phenomenological and experimental sides. Here, the focus is on an experimental counterpart to recent phenomenological work on the $D$-measure of net-charge fluctuations: how restricted detector acceptance in rapidity and transverse momentum can be controlled experimentally. We demonstrate this for the second-order net-charge cumulant, $\kappa_2(\Delta Q)$, by rewriting it in terms of the charge balance function and the charged-particle rapidity density. Both are event-averaged observables for which experimental efficiency corrections and extrapolations into unmeasured kinematic regions can be studied systematically. This provides a complementary experimental route for connecting measurements of $D = 4\kappa_2(\Delta Q)/\langle N_{ch} \rangle$ to theory and a possible starting point for extending the same strategy to the fourth-order cumulant.
item.dc:creator: Peter Christiansen

item.title: Tracing Electromagnetic Response through Charge Splitting of Directed Flow in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
item.description: arXiv:2610.38363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Experimentally observed charge splitting of directed flow, $\Delta v_1\equiv v_1(h^+)-v_1(h^-)$, exhibits both a sign reversal at midrapidity and the amplitude change from Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV to Pb+Pb at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We study this behavior within a unified $(3+1)$-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic model that incorporates an electromagnetic source term in the bulk evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and an electromagnetic correction to the Cooper--Frye particlization. The beam-energy dependence of $\Delta v_1$ can be described by varying the effective electrical conductivity between RHIC and LHC energies, with values consistent with the conductivity scale indicated by lattice-QCD calculations. We find that the sign reversal emerges from the competition between momentum distortions induced by the electric and magnetic field which is controlled by the conductivity during the QGP evolution. The model further predicts the mass-dependent charge splittings for identified pions, kaons, and protons, providing further constraints on their respective relaxation times and the corresponding electromagnetic interaction. These results establish the charge splitting of directed flow as a quantitative probe of the electromagnetic response and the space-time evolution of the QGP.
item.dc:creator: Ankit Kumar Panda, Zhu Meng, Long-Gang Pang, Xin-Nian Wang

item.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.38463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and in the loop sum. Retaining the refined Gribov-Zwanziger masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, retaining contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and by the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms close the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite answer is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not assume colored asymptotic states or establish an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.
item.dc:creator: Wan Wu

item.title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.38571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Jin Hu

item.title: Collinear Factorization and Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.38666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The method of collinear factorization for high-energy inclusive cross sections has found wide use in the analysis of hadronic collisions. We introduce the form of factorized cross sections, and discuss the roles and definitions of parton distributions, hadronic fragmentation functions, and their evolution, starting with parton model concepts. The Drell-Yan process is used to illustrate the calculation of QCD corrections at next-to-leading order. The special role of deep-inelastic scattering structure functions and their relation to hadronic structure are also briefly discussed. We provide an introduction to all-order arguments for factorization and infrared safety, and close with a brief review of related factorization formalisms.
item.dc:creator: George Sterman, Zhite Yu

item.title: Precision Studies of Boosted Polarized Vector Bosons with Energy Correlators
item.description: arXiv:2610.38688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Boosted, hadronically decaying $W$ and $Z$ bosons are among the most abundant heavy objects at colliders, and their vector nature makes their substructure qualitatively richer than that of a scalar. We initiate precision studies of the hadronic decays of boosted polarized vector bosons with energy correlators. In the narrow-width limit, the laboratory-frame two-point energy correlator is a sum of longitudinal and transverse decay spectra, each weighted by its polarized production rate and obtained by a closed-form boost kernel acting on rest-frame correlators. Combining polarized production density matrices, computed at NNLO in QCD for $pp\to V+X$ and at leading order for $e^+e^-\to W^+W^-$, with decay correlators that combine NNLO fixed order with NNLL collinear and N$^4$LL back-to-back resummation, we find for high-$p_T$ $W/Z$ production that polarization shifts the spectrum by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ relative to a naive unpolarized treatment. Even without any reconstruction, hadronic $W/Z$ decays stand out over the realistic QCD background of untagged jet samples as a localized angular bump. Our results open the door to using energy correlators for polarimetry of electroweak bosons through their hadronic decays, for standard-candle measurements of electroweak bosons inside jets, and in sharper searches for new resonances.
item.dc:creator: Anjie Gao, Kyle Lee, Xiaoyuan Zhang

item.title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
item.description: arXiv:2610.39128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.
item.dc:creator: Josuke Minamiguchi, Tomoya Uji

item.title: Muon-to-positron conversion from light Majorana neutrino exchange: nuclear responses and pion-pole-improved multipoles
item.description: arXiv:2610.39135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study muon-to-positron conversion in nuclei that is mediated by light Majorana neutrinos, which probes lepton-number violation in the electron-muon sector. As the second paper in a series, this work extends our study of local dimension-nine interactions to the mass mechanism. We derive the conversion amplitude from the second-order effective four-Fermi interaction and express it in terms of nuclear responses in the one-body impulse approximation. Using phenomenological nucleon form factors, we retain convection, axial charge, weak magnetism, and the longitudinal pion-pole current in a specified pion-pole-improved prescription. The two physical time orderings and the distinct momentum transfers are derived in the intermediate-state response. We complete its angular reduction and derive the corresponding closure operator, including spin-gradient terms. Both the symmetric (scalar) and antisymmetric (vector) lepton-hadron Lorentz contractions contribute to the spin-averaged, angle-integrated rate. For $0^+\!\to0^+$ transitions we give explicit formulas in terms of two coherent radial amplitudes, without restricting the intermediate nuclei to spin zero. This provides an interface to nuclear calculations of the required nuclear matrix elements. However, in this work, no isotope-specific numerical predictions are attempted. The present treatment uses approximate lepton wavefunctions and recoil-free nuclear propagation. Two-body weak currents and systematic chiral effective-field-theory matching are left for future work.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liao, Hao-Lin Wang

item.title: Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.39402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $\Delta(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.
item.dc:creator: Probit J Kalita, Subha Mitra, Bharat Kumar

item.title: The effect of Coulomb interaction on Levy source parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.39626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Femtoscopy plays an important role in the study of heavy-ion collisions and particle sources generated within them. In both experimental measurements and theoretical models, a L\'evy distribution is used to describe the shape of the source, as the Gaussian distribution has proven to be inaccurate based on experimental observations. Despite this, there are still discrepancies between experimental data and the results of theoretical models. One reason may be that these theoretical models either approximate the Coulomb interaction poorly or omit it entirely. In our research, we focused on how the Coulomb effect influences the stability index $\alpha$ value of the L\'evy distribution. For this, we used a custom-developed simulation framework written in C++ and Python. The C++ module integrates the equations of motion for relativistic pions using the Leapfrog algorithm, while the Python post-processing script generates the two-particle spatial source function from the phase-space coordinates. We investigate the ratio and slope of the generated and pair-source fitted $\alpha$ as a function of the number of particles, fitting range, and the initial source size and density.
item.dc:creator: Kristof Csiki, Mate Csanad, Barnabas Porfy

item.title: $P$--wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2610.39959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $\chi_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $\chi_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $\chi_{cJ}$ and $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.
item.dc:creator: Taewook Ha, Byungsik Hong, Daekyoung Kang, Soohwan Lee, Bayu Adi Nugraha Putra

item.title: Sizeable mixing between the coexisting normal and intruder structures of $^{96}$Zr revealed through lifetime measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.40037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lifetimes of excited states of the nucleus $^{96}$Zr were studied with the Doppler-shift attenuation method following the $^{94}$Zr($^{18}$O,$^{16}$O)$^{96}$Zr two-neutron transfer reaction. The obtained $B(E2;2^+_2\to0^+_2)$ and $B(E2;4^+_1\to2^+_2)$ transition strengths, amounting to $26(2)$ and $39(7)$\,W.u., respectively, firmly attribute the $2^+_2$ and $4^+_1$ states to the collective intruder band built on top of the $0^+_2$ state. The nature of this structure is discussed against predictions of the collective model using the Bohr Hamiltonian, the interacting boson model with configuration mixing, and the quasiparticle vacua shell model. The collective, interband $B(E2;4^+_1\to2^+_1)=11.2(8)$\,W.u. transition strength, refuting the previously assumed purity of both structures, is reproduced in the calculations. The quasiparticle vacua shell model predicts, in agreement with a simple two-state model based on experimental $E2$ transition strengths, considerable mixing between the normal and intruder $2^+$ states.

M\u{a}rginean, H. Mayr, C. Mihai, R. E. Mihai, A. Mitu, C. R. Nita, T. Otsuka, O. Papst, S. Pascu, C. Sotty, L. Stan, S. Toma, Y. Tsunoda, A. Turturic\u{a}, S. Ujeniuc, J. Wiederhold

item.title: Inverse Problem Approach for Non-Perturbative QCD: Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.40111v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In arXiv:2211.13753 we proposed a novel theoretical approach for non-perturbative QCD, named the inverse problem approach. It extracts non-perturbative quantities by solving a dispersion integral equation as an inverse problem, using perturbative QCD and operator product expansion as inputs. In this work, we apply this approach to the pion and $a_1(1260)$ decay constants, as well as the continuum spectral function. The extracted $f_\pi = 130.8 \pm 8.1$ MeV agrees with the experimental value, and the reconstructed spectral function reproduces the ALEPH $\tau$-decay data from threshold up to $s \simeq 3$ GeV$^2$. The advantages of this approach are as follows: (i) the whole non-perturbative range is solved simultaneously, yielding the ground state, excited states, and the continuum spectrum within a single framework; (ii) it is based on rigorous mathematics, with not only statistical but also systematic uncertainties well controlled and quantifiable; (iii) the regularized solutions exhibit convergence, allowing the precision to be systematically improved with better inputs; (iv) quark-hadron duality emerges naturally at high energy scales, avoiding the low-energy duality assumption and the Borel transformation, and eliminating their associated uncertainties. Finally, the successful physical application of the inverse problem approach demonstrates its broad applicability to non-perturbative quantities.
item.dc:creator: Yong Zheng, Ao-Sheng Xiong, Fu-Sheng Yu, Ting Wei

item.title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
item.description: arXiv:2610.40220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.
item.dc:creator: Rasmus Normann Larsen, Peter Petreczky, Jorge Luis Dasilva Golan, Johannes H. Weber

item.title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Locating the minimum of a nuclear collective landscape can require many interacting many-body calculations. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family with a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle. The oracle supplies the predicate required for quantum minimum-finding without first constructing the energy landscape point by point. We implement it for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model using circuit-generated energy estimates during the search. In a four-point calculation, one Grover round raises the probability of the true minimum from 0.25 to 0.921. A $4\times4$ quadrupole--octupole-field calculation extends the complete circuit to two coordinates, although its minimum is first sampled in a round with zero Grover iterations. Its worst-case branch-preparation fidelity of 0.744 falls below the declared target, identifying coherent ground-state access as the current bottleneck. QDMin inherits expected $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ candidate-query scaling in the unstructured model; total advantage depends on the many-body oracle cost and remains unestablished.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek, P. Arumugam

item.title: Typed Transverse Momentum Parton distribution function computations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution enters an extraction through a specified observation map and a parameter- dependent numerical calculation. Equal units and matching array dimensions do not establish that two implementations represent the same inference problem. We present typed-TMD, a computational framework that makes observation semantics, parameter dependencies, and admissible evaluation plans explicit.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Keller

item.title: Parameter adjustment of nuclear leading-order local pairing energy density functionals
item.description: arXiv:2603.13164v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: (See paper for full abstract) This study reports on the benchmarking of a protocol for the adjustment of the parameters of a local leading-order (LO) T=1 (like-particle) pairing EDF that consists in adjusting the density-dependence of the 1S0 pairing gap at the chemical potential in infinite nuclear matter (INM). When using a suitably chosen reference calculation, this protocol leads to consistent results for the odd-even staggering of masses of spherical and heavy deformed nuclei and also for the rotational moments of inertia calculated in a time-reversal-breaking cranked HFB approach. The implementation of the HFB solver for infinite matter at arbitrary isospin asymmetry used for this study is sketched in appendices. Additional points that are discussed concern (i) the illustration that the gaps at the chemical potential are not necessarily sufficient to completely characterise the pairing interaction in infinite matter, and that adjusting LO pairing EDF to reproduce gaps obtained from finite-range pairing interactions in HFB or from more microscopic calculations can lead to unrealistic predictions for finite nuclei; (ii) the finding that some regions of the parameter space for the density dependence of the T=1 LO pairing EDF lead to a spurious transition to a Bose-Einstein condensate of di-nucleons in spite of producing realistic pairing correlations for well-bound nuclei; (iii) the correlation between effective mass and the parameters of the LO pairing EDF that control the form factor of the density dependence when reproducing pairing gaps in infinite matter, (iv) the significant impact on the odd-even staggering of masses made by either including or not the spin-gradient terms in the particle-hole part of the Skyrme EDF; (v) the sizeable impact of keeping or not the contribution from the density-dependent LO pairing EDF to the mean fields on the odd-even staggering of radii.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bender, Karim Bennaceur, Valentin Guillon

item.title: A short-range effective theory for single-neutron halo nuclei with a deformed core
item.description: arXiv:2606.21547v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a short-range effective theory for deformed s-wave halos. The theory applies to a system in which neutrons are weakly bound to a core nucleus, and that core nucleus also exhibits a low-lying rotational band with a $0^+$ ground state and a first $2_1^+$ excited state. The effective theory then must have both halo degrees of freedom and degrees of freedom associated with rotation of the core. This leads to the particle plus rotor model of Bohr and Mottelson at leading order. We identify the relevant leading-order operators in the Hamiltonian that respect the symmetries of the system and the small parameters which define the effective theory's power counting. We carry out calculations for the $^{11}$Be and $^{17}$C systems in which we compute the low-lying positive-parity states of the core $+$ neutron systems up to the core$(2_1^+)$-neutron threshold. We do this for several different regulator parameters and establish that these energies can be renormalized using the leading-order set of operators. The spectrum is accurately described at leading order in both cases. Decay widths to d-wave core-neutron states have sizable cutoff dependence, but the Asymptotic Normalization Coefficients (ANCs) in $s$-wave channels exhibit regulator dependence of a size consistent with next-to-leading-order effects. We also compute Coulomb breakup observables and compare with experimental data, finding leading-order results in reasonable agreement with data for both ${}^{11}$Be and ${}^{17}$C. The addition of one next-to-leading-order operator renders the ANCs of all s-wave states stable with respect to the regulator. It consequently also removes most of the 30\% variation of the leading-order Coulomb dissociation cross section with the regulator.
item.dc:creator: Live-Palm Kubushishi, Daniel R. Phillips

item.title: Comprehensive study of $\Upsilon$($n$S) production in Oxygen+Oxygen collisions at LHC
item.description: arXiv:2609.16292v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bottomonium $\Upsilon$($n$S) production in ${\rm O}+{\rm O}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.36$~TeV, including both cold nuclear-matter (CNM) effects and final-state interactions in a short-lived quark-gluon plasma. The CNM baseline is calculated using the EPPS21 nuclear parton distribution functions together with coherent energy loss and transverse momentum broadening. Hot-medium effects are evaluated with two transport approaches coupled to the same centrality-resolved 3+1D aHydroQP background: the QTRAJ-NLO open-quantum-system calculation, implemented with the {\sc QTraj} code, and the TAMU-NP semiclassical rates, including primordial suppression and regeneration. The CNM effects give a moderate, state-independent suppression, dominated by the nPDF modification. The energy loss and transverse momentum broadening contribution remains at the few-percent level. Both transport approaches predict a sequential suppression pattern, $R_{AA}^{\Upsilon(1\rm{S})}>R_{AA}^{\Upsilon(2\rm{S})}>R_{AA}^{\Upsilon(3\rm{S})}$, with the strongest suppression around midrapidity in central collisions. The suppression of the ground state is similar in the two approaches but differs for the excited states. Since the CNM factor is common to all states, double ratios provide a direct measure of the relative hot-medium suppression. Our results support the conclusion that ${\rm O}+{\rm O}$ collisions at the LHC can produce a short-lived QGP capable of modifying bottomonium yields.
item.dc:creator: Sabin Thapa, Biaogang Wu, Ramona Vogt, Ralf Rapp

item.title: Systematic Study of Proton, Two-Proton, Alpha, and Cluster Radioactivity Half-Lives based on the Deformed Gamow-like Model and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$)
item.description: arXiv:2609.21646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A hybrid framework combining the deformed Gamow-like model ($\mathrm{DGLM}$) with the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$) is developed to improve half-life predictions for two-proton emission, proton emission, $\alpha$ decay, and cluster radioactivity. A total of 583 radioactive nuclei are investigated, including 17 two-proton emitters, 42 proton emitters, 498 $\alpha$ emitters, and 26 cluster emitters. Among the four considered models, $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}+\mathrm{TabPFN}$ achieves the best overall performance, with $\sigma_{\mathrm{RMS}}=0.423$, corresponding to an improvement of approximately $82.2\%$ over $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}$. The model parameters are optimized for each decay mode using the least-squares method. After introducing $\mathrm{TabPFN}$, the prediction errors for proton emission and $\alpha$ decay are reduced by approximately $80.6\%$ and $87.6\%$, respectively. For $\alpha$ decay, the training, test, and overall RMSEs are 0.208, 0.305, and 0.240, indicating good generalization capability without evident overfitting. The model also reproduces the systematic evolution of $\alpha$-decay half-lives and the shell-closure effect around $N=126$. These results demonstrate that combining $\mathrm{DGLM}$ with $\mathrm{TabPFN}$ significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of radioactive-decay half-life predictions while retaining the physical interpretability of the original model.
item.dc:creator: Anqi Yang, Panpan Qi, Qingning Yuan, Gongming Yu, Haitao Yang, Zhangyan Li, Yanbing Cai

item.title: Structure of QC$_2$D ground state fields at nonzero matter densities
item.description: arXiv:2603.22825v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A quantitative investigation into the modification of ground-state field structures in two-color QCD (QC$_2$D) is presented at finite chemical potential. Using lattice simulations with Wilson gauge and fermion actions, we explore the chromo-electromagnetic field strengths under varying matter densities. To ensure accurate measurements, we develop and calibrate two highly improved topological charge operators and evaluate four gradient flow actions. Our results reveal a finite-volume crossover in the regime of the anticipated phase boundary at $\mu = m_\pi/2$, with both chromoelectric and chromomagnetic field strengths suppressed before recovering and exceeding vacuum values at higher chemical potentials. We find the difference between the squared chromoelectric and chromomagnetic field strengths, $E^2-B^2$, to increase in magnitude monotonically with increasing chemical potential. At $a\mu=0.7$, we find an $11\%$ suppression of $E^2$, a relatively small effect. A systematic analysis using sigmoid fits of lattice simulations in the crossover regime is performed to confirm the critical chemical potential obtained from the field structure is in agreement with the phase boundary at $m_\pi / 2$. These findings provide new insight into non-Abelian ground-state vacuum field structures and offer a foundation for future studies in real QCD.
item.dc:creator: Ragib F. Hasan, Matthew Cummins, Waseem Kamleh, Dale Lawlor, Derek Leinweber, Ian van Schalkwyk, Jon-Ivar Skullerud

item.title: Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
item.description: arXiv:2603.26973v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Legred, Nicolas Yunes

item.title: Finite temperature effects on g-modes of inviscid neutron stars
item.description: arXiv:2604.11815v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the effect of temperature on secular, compositional $g$-modes in the core of inviscid neutron stars. Using a chiral $SU(2)_f$ sigma model, we construct isentropic temperature profiles for hot and dense matter and find that the frequency of the global core $g$-mode's dependence on temperature is governed by the nuclear symmetry energy slope parameter $L$. As a result, the $g$-mode frequency of a warm neutron star can be either higher or lower than that of its cold counterpart, depending on $L$. Our results highlight the interplay of thermal effects and composition gradients, and demonstrate the potential of neutron star $g$-mode observations to constrain the density dependence of the symmetry energy.
item.dc:creator: David Morales-Zapien, Prashanth Jaikumar, Thomas Kl\"ahn

item.title: Short-range correlated pair formation and nuclear shell structure
item.description: arXiv:2606.07754v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Short-range correlated (SRC) nucleon pairs, caused by brief, high-momentum interactions between two nucleons, are dominated by neutron-proton pairs with large relative and smaller center-of-mass momenta. However, which nucleons form pairs is not fully understood. Measurements of 40,48Ca and 54Fe showed that intra-shell pairing was much stronger than inter-shell pairing. We measured high- missing-momentum protons knocked out in electron scattering from selected nuclei with a range of shell configurations, A, and N/Z, including 9Be, 10,11B, 12C, 40,48Ca, 54Fe, and 197Au, focusing on the four light nuclei. Unexpectedly, we found that adding one proton to 9Be (to make 10B) increased the number of correlated protons far more than adding one neutron to 10B or adding one proton to 11B, perhaps due to the large spin (J = 3) of 10B or the unusual structure of 9Be. In addition, the increase in pairing probability from 9Be to 12C and from 40Ca to 54Fe was much steeper than the increase from 9Be to 197Au. This shows the importance of low-momentum nuclear structure on the probability of high-momentum nucleon pairing.
item.dc:creator: D. Nguyen, C. Yero, H. Szumila-Vance, F. Hauenstein, N. Swan, L. B. Weinstein, J. Kahlbow, A. Schmidt, E. Piasetzky, O. Hen, C. Ayerbe Gayoso, E. Cohen, P. Datta, A. Denniston, B. R. Devkota, M. Diefenthaler, C. Fogler, B. R. Gamage, D. Higinbotham, I. Korover, C. Morean, M. Nycz, M. Satnik, S. Seeds, P. Sharp, I. Shlush, M. Suresh, A. S. Tadepalli, R. Wagner, E. W. Wertz

item.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30393v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.
item.dc:creator: Bruno S. Lopes, Arthur E. B. Pasqualotto, Jandir J. Buttenbender Filho, Dyana C. Duarte, Ricardo L. S. Farias
